views.concept: system context: the machine manager as ONE ordinary box in its world

attempts.label: l0-a-four-exits
attempts.design: eight nodes, no container: callers left (cp, web, agent), the manager box in the middle, the four things it talks to on the right (providers, machines, S3, Slack), seven coarse arrows, four of them leaving the manager's right side
lever_sweep: no lever: 1 ambiguous label owner (l0:e5 'images + diagnostics')
layers pin ['prov','mch','slack','s3']: unchanged, 1 ambiguous (layers pins ranks, not sibling order)
empty slots in the layer ('mch','','prov','','s3','','slack'): unchanged, 1 ambiguous
label_slot on the S3 edge: the S3 label is owned, the tie moves to 'provider API'
label_slot on all four right-side exits: 'provider API' gets no free slot at all
attempts.verdict: rejected: a manager box with four exits packs ports one row apart, so one label always ties with a neighbouring route. Measured: labels: 7/7 placed, 1 ambiguous owner.

attempts.label: l0-b-short-labels
attempts.design: same four-exit design with every arrow label shortened to one or two words (provisions / http / heartbeat / provider API / boot + audit / boot image / alerts)
attempts.verdict: rejected: still 1 ambiguous owner ('provider API'); label length does not break the tie, the port spacing does

attempts.label: l0-c-three-exits
attempts.design: the manager keeps three exits only (provider API, boot + audit, confirm + alerts); S3 is reached by the machines it serves ('pull boot image' is that source relation, drawn at its most-fitting level), so mch->s3 lives on L0 and L1 no longer redraws it. label_slot on the middle exit (provider API).
attempts.verdict: SHIPPED: 7/7 labels placed, 0 ambiguous, 0 near-misses, 0 skipped

views.concept: the manager opened one level: its boundary services inside a labelled box, the externals outside

attempts.label: l1-a-carried-nine-edges
attempts.design: the liked previous L1 block carried unchanged: eleven nodes, container on six boundary services, five pinned ranks, nine edges including mch->s3
attempts.verdict: clean check (0 near-misses, 0 ambiguous labels) but mch->s3 must not be drawn twice once L0 carries it, so the block changed for the coverage rule, not for a layout defect

attempts.label: l1-b-s3-moved-out
attempts.design: ten nodes, eight edges: the S3 corner removed (mch->s3 is on L0), container unchanged, five pinned ranks, externals cp/web/prov/mch outside the box

views.concept: the machine side: the fleet's own outward relations

attempts.label: l1b-a-carried
attempts.design: the liked previous L1b block unchanged: seven nodes, container on q/wapi/pub, four pinned ranks, four edges
attempts.verdict: SHIPPED unchanged: 4/4 labels placed, 0 ambiguous, 0 near-misses

views.concept: the manager's inside: the container relationships

attempts.label: l2-a-merged-pinned
attempts.design: ONE diagram for all ten internal relations (nine nodes) with three pinned-rank orderings: [wapi,pgrpc,pub,rec]|[q]|[reg,ssh,jan,db]; [pgrpc,wapi]|[q,pub,rec]|[reg,ssh,jan,db]; [wapi,pub,rec,pgrpc]|[q]|[jan,reg,ssh,db]
attempts.verdict: rejected: every pinning fails validation with 'no obstacle-safe route for jan -> wapi' (the wapi->q->jan->wapi cycle has to cross the queue's rank)

attempts.label: l2-b-merged-auto
attempts.design: the same nine-node merged diagram with the engine's own ranking (no pins)
attempts.verdict: rejected: it routes, but with passes-near-unrelated-node: 14 (route l2:e4 hugs 'pub' and 'rec') and 1 ambiguous label owner, both rubric failures

attempts.label: l2-c-split-yield
attempts.design: the L2 level yields to two diagrams, exactly the shapes the owner liked: L2 (queue and dispatch, six edges) and L2b (the state writes into Postgres, four edges). Every one of the ten internal relations is drawn once.
attempts.verdict: SHIPPED: 10/10 labels placed across the two diagrams, 0 ambiguous, 0 near-misses. Evidenced yield, records above.
